report.scope: Actual disposable-owner GDM/PAM login and normal GNOME virtual DRM/input session observation. Synthetic credential only in memory/private transient channel. No autologin or session-policy bypass; selected application actions need their own evidence; no B02/physical completion.

verified_selected_actions: Selected actual GDM test-user card; typed a random private password only after visually checking the masked password field; normal PAM login yielded active seat0/user/Wayland session2.

GNOME overview search text and Return launched the installed unmodified Text Editor. Real typing and save dialog worked. A too-fast chord/typing sequence produced an unintended short filename and trailing text; corrected by ordinary select-all/edit/save with explicit post-chord delays.
Saved home file toddy-pr, quit/relaunched the editor, observed the restored correct text without unsaved indicator; actual maximize-button pointer click preserved readable content.

Overview search launched Settings; Network panel accurately showed NetworkManager not running. Pointer navigation opened Appearance and selected the Dark tile. Global theme propagation was not verified.
Overview search launched Terminal; actual PTY/Bash accepted whoami, cat toddy-pr and sha256sum toddy-pr. Screenshot shows user toddy-preview, file contents and the independently matched SHA256.

saved_file_observation.observation_source: Actual native Terminal screenshot, matched independently on the host; no direct filesystem export in this slice.

limitations: Editor refusal/crash recovery and post-reboot persistence not tested here.
Settings selected Dark tile but both GTK4 windows still appeared light; global theme propagation unqualified.
NetworkManager was inactive; actual network/audio/privileged storage functions remain pending.

Terminal still uses stock bash-5.3 prompt; lightweight user-preserving navy defaults remain pending.

Synthetic account and its files existed only in the now-stopped disposable overlay; no installed production user was created.
